previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with inoperable cholangiocarcinoma and a history of recurrent cholangitis, was admitted with fever, chills, and nausea. He was started on empiric IV meropenem and vancomycin, though vancomycin was discontinued given negative blood cultures and low MRSA risk. Imaging revealed persistent cholangitis with pneumobilia limiting assessment, but no new biliary obstruction. Due to prior hemobilia, ERCP was deferred. A 10-day course of meropenem was planned via PICC line, with transition to oral doxycycline and Bactrim for infection suppression. His pancytopenia remained stable and within baseline. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with home IV antibiotics and follow-up arranged with oncology and infectious disease.
problems: Benign prostatic hyperplasia without lower urinary tract symptoms

EXAMINATION:  CT ABDOMEN PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ w/ recurrent bacteremia, ? of biliary source vs colonic as
new onset transient diarrhea// please evaluate the biliary system for
potential source of bacteremia and colonic wall     patient has a history of
cholangiocarcinoma on surveillance.

TECHNIQUE:   Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were
acquired through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast
administration with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Sequenced Acquisition 0.5 s, 0.4 cm; CTDIvol = 4.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 1.9
mGy-cm.
   2) Stationary Acquisition 27.6 s, 0.2 cm; CTDIvol = 470.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
94.0 mGy-cm.
   3) Spiral Acquisition 8.7 s, 56.4 cm; CTDIvol = 11.4 mGy (Body) DLP = 634.5
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 730 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___, MRCP ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: There is left greater than right bibasilar atelectasis.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: As seen previously, the left lobe of the liver is atrophic. 
There is persistent moderate left biliary duct dilation and mild right
intrahepatic biliary duct dilation most pronounced in segment V.  The right
and common hepatic stents are unchanged and appear to be in appropriate
position.  There is a small amount of pneumobilia, as expected.  The known
cholangiocarcinoma is not discretely seen on the current study.  No focal
hepatic lesions are seen.  The gallbladder is decompressed and air filled.

PANCREAS: Unchanged morphology of the pancreas which demonstrates mild diffuse
atrophy and dilation of the pancreatic duct most pronounced in the head where
it measures up to 0.6 cm.  There is no peripancreatic abnormality.

SPLEEN: The spleen is enlarged measuring 15.8 cm.  There are few scattered
calcifications within the spleen which likely reflect prior granulomatous
infection.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is a simple cyst in the interpolar left kidney measuring 1.0 cm.

GASTROINTESTINAL: There is a small hiatal hernia.  There is no bowel
obstruction.  A few scattered diverticular noted in the sigmoid colon without
evidence of diverticulitis.  Large bowel is unremarkable.  The appendix is not
visualized but there are no secondary signs of appendicitis in the right lower
quadrant.  There is no intra-abdominal free fluid or free air.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The prostate is enlarged measuring approximately 3.8 x
5.1 x 5.1 cm with an estimated volume of 51 cc.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.  The main and right portal veins are patent.  The left portal vein
is attenuated but appears patent.

BONES: Multilevel degenerative changes are noted.  There is no evidence of
worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. No CT evidence of acute intra-abdominal and pelvic process.
2. Similar morphology of the intrahepatic bile ducts with moderate left and
mild right ductal dilation.  Known intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is not
discretely seen.  Common bile duct stents are appropriately positioned.
3. Stable splenomegaly.
4. Diverticulosis.
